question: Does fixing our own RNG seeding (worker hash seed on AGI-2, sha256 game seed on AGI-3) reduce leaderboard run-to-run variance? Prior identical-code spreads: AGI-2 1.67 pts over 5 samples (mis-seeded v4); AGI-3 14x over 7 samples (mis-seeded v2). Each seeded version has n=1. A second sample of each separates our randomness from Kaggle's.

predeclared_reading.agi2: If |v11#2 - 29.31| <= 0.5, seeding accounts for most of the prior spread and the board's resolution floor drops below 2 pts. If >= 1.5, the variance is Kaggle-side and the floor stands.
predeclared_reading.agi3: If v4#2 is within 2x of 0.03, our RNG was the dominant source. If it lands anywhere in 0.10-0.18, the 14x spread is Kaggle-side (hidden-instance or environment randomness) and no local seeding can fix it.
